title: Houses of worship protected
hookLine: permission to defend is given, for otherwise monasteries, churches, synagogues and mosques would be pulled down (22:39–40)

lines: THE REASON IS A LIST OF BUILDINGS.
cards: In Mecca, the early Muslims were mocked, boycotted and harmed. Through all of it, they were told to be patient and not to strike back. Then they left their homes and went north to Medina.
Around that time, according to commentators, came the first verses that gave permission to fight back. What's striking is the reason the verses give. It isn't only, you've been wronged.

teach.h: DRIVEN OUT FOR SAYING: OUR LORD IS GOD.
teach.b: Verse thirty-nine says permission is given to those who are fought against, because they have been wronged. Verse forty describes them: people driven from their homes unjustly, only because they said, our Lord is God.
Then it explains why such permission exists at all.

If God did not check some people by means of others, Pickthall says, "cloisters and churches and oratories and mosques, wherein the name of Allah is oft mentioned, would assuredly have been pulled down."
Four kinds of building, in Arabic: sawami', biya', salawat, masajid.

Commentators explain them roughly this way: sawami' are the retreats of monks and hermits; biya' are churches; salawat, in a common reading, are the prayer houses of the Jews; and masajid are mosques.

teach.h: THE MOSQUE COMES LAST IN THE LIST.
teach.b: The mosque comes last in the list.

The phrase, where the name of God is often remembered, sits over all four; commentators differ on whether it belongs to the mosques alone or to every house in the list, and some take it the wider way.
And this list sits in the very verse that first allows a persecuted community to defend itself.

The reason given isn't only: protect your own. It's that without some check on oppression, places of prayer of every kind come down. History offers plenty of examples where that ideal was broken, by people of many faiths.
The verse still stands as a measure. A defense that pulls down a church or a synagogue has forgotten the reason it was permitted in the first place.

how: Muslim scholars and community leaders often cite 22:40 when speaking about the protection of places of worship, including after attacks on churches, synagogues, temples and mosques.

the churches named second in that list of buildings

p: prayer houses, often read as the Jews'

games.q: a community driven from its homes is finally given permission to defend itself. what reason does the verse give?
o: to take back what was lost, and more.
so that houses of prayer of every kind aren't pulled down.
so that the community can grow larger.
games.why: the verse gives a list: cloisters, churches, oratories and mosques. the reason is the protection of worship itself.

practice: Picture the places of worship near where you live, a mosque, a church, a synagogue, a temple, a gurdwara, a small room where people meet to pray, full of people on a Friday, a Saturday, a Sunday.
If you pray, you can ask for their protection, all of them. If you don't, simply wish them safety.

wordCard.voice: Masajid. Mosques, named last in 22:40's list of houses of worship, cloisters, churches, oratories and mosques, protected together. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: prayers; in 22:40 commentators often read it as the prayer houses of the Jews.

carryVoice: Your line: all houses of prayer protected. The mosque is named last, beside the rest. Four hundred eighty-eight days now.
